The Crucial T710 is a solid-state drive in the M.2 2280 form factor, launched on May 19th, 2025. It is available in capacities ranging from 1 TB to 4 TB. This page reports specifications for the 2 TB variant. With the rest of the system, the Crucial T710 interfaces using a PCI-Express 5.0 x4 connection. The SSD controller is the SM2508 from Silicon Motion, a DRAM cache chip is available. Crucial has installed 276-layer TLC NAND flash on the T710, the flash chips are made by Micron. To improve write speeds, a pseudo-SLC cache is used, so bursts of incoming writes are processed more quickly. The cache is sized at 368 GB, once it is full, writes complete at 4,000 MB/s. Copying data out of the SLC cache (folding) completes at 1,950 MB/s. Thanks to support for the fast PCI-Express 5.0 interface, performance is excellent. The T710 is rated for sequential read speeds of up to 14,500 MB/s and 13,800 MB/s write; random IOPS reach up to 2200K for reads and 2300K for writes. At its launch, the SSD was priced at 280 USD. The warranty length is set to five years, which is an excellent warranty period. Crucial guarantees an endurance rating of 1200 TBW, a typical value for consumer SSDs.
